chunks: The station of Ibrāhīm عليه السلام came to be on its left because Ibrāhīm عليه السلام has a station on the Day of Resurrection, and Muḥammad صلى الله عليه وآله has a station. So the station of Muḥammad صلى الله عليه وآله is on the right of the Throne of our Lord, Mighty and Majestic, and the station of Ibrāhīm عليه السلام is on the left of His Throne. Thus, the station of Ibrāhīm عليه السلام is in accordance with his station on the Day of Resurrection, while the Throne of our Lord, Blessed and Exalted, faces forward, not turned away.
And the Syrian Corner came to be moving in winter and summer, and by night and day, because the wind is confined beneath it.

And the House only came to be elevated, with ascent to it by steps, because when al-Ḥajjāj demolished the Kaʿbah, the people dispersed its soil. Then when they wanted to build it, a serpent came out against them and prevented the people from building. So al-Ḥajjāj was approached and informed, and al-Ḥajjāj asked ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn عليهما السلام about that, and he said to him: ‘Order the people that no one among them who took anything from it should remain except that he returns it.’ Then when its walls were raised, he ordered the soil, and it was cast into its interior. For that reason the House came to be elevated, with ascent to it by steps.

And the people came to circumambulate around the Ḥijr and not circumambulate within it because the mother of Ismāʿīl was buried in the Ḥijr, and her grave is there. So circumambulation was made in that manner so that her grave would not be trodden upon.

key_terms.الرُّكْنُ الشَّامِيُّ: The Syrian Corner of the Kaʿbah, described here as moving because of wind beneath it.
key_terms.الْبَيْتُ: The Kaʿbah, described as elevated after its reconstruction.
key_terms.الْحِجْرِ: The enclosed area near the Kaʿbah around which people perform ṭawāf and within which the grave of Ismāʿīl's mother is said to be.
key_terms.الْقِيَامَةِ: The Day of Resurrection, in which the stations of Ibrāhīm and Muḥammad صلى الله عليه وآله are described.
key_terms.الْكَعْبَةَ: The Kaʿbah, whose destruction and rebuilding are referenced in the report.
key_terms.عَرْشِ: The Throne, mentioned as the reference point for the stations of Muḥammad صلى الله عليه وآله and Ibrāhīm عليه السلام.
key_terms.مَقَامُ إِبْرَاهِيمَ: The station of Ibrāhīm عليه السلام, whose location is linked here to his eschatological station.

ai.seo_question: Why is Maqām Ibrāhīm placed to the left, why is the Kaʿbah elevated, and why do people perform ṭawāf around al-Ḥijr?
ai.summary: This report explains several features connected to the Kaʿbah and hajj through their spiritual and historical causes. It links Maqām Ibrāhīm to stations in the Hereafter, describes the elevation of the Kaʿbah after its rebuilding, and explains why ṭawāf is performed around al-Ḥijr rather than inside it.
